accepted_findings.conclusion: Both new booleans use serde(default) and Rust Default=false. Omitting the options preserves the default source-admission policy; the switches remain independent.

Known-language and explicit-include paths retain their existing selection. Newly admitted generic text is bounded by the configured file limit plus one-byte overflow detection and must be UTF-8 without NUL. This is not a claim of AST support or content validation for every recognized-language input.

Either broad option enables the shared protected path policy in final source admission and event ignore rules. Clearing the user ignore list does not override it. The source-only scoped walk retains protected-path pruning.

Broad source admission rejects final file symlinks. The scoped walk is anchored at the real project root and uses the ignore walker default of not following directory symlinks; the examined source does not support a parent-symlink bypass claim.

The changed event predicate extends tracking to opted-in hidden source while still applying IgnoreRules. Existing project-model configuration candidates continue to bypass source-only ignores so cache invalidation is not accidentally treated as source chunk admission.

The five PR153 integration methods exercise real full/directory/single-event scanner agreement, independent defaults, generic content and byte limits, a symlink alias, and actual parser/SQLite/FTS update, move, delete, and binary-transition behavior. Two watcher methods exercise real notify event classification and protected/user-ignore decisions. No existing assertion was relaxed by this review.

limits: This review covers the original four paths above, not the independent MCP readiness changes, Python registry/data integration, full CI, hidden-source completeness, or any original TODO acceptance.
The published PR153 source identity was reviewed statically. Red/green runtime receipts bind their own exact merged local commit; they are not relabeled as execution on the original PR153 head.
Original local P615 failures remain recorded; no source-integrity or previous benchmark result is transferred to a new merged source identity.
scope: non-author review of the original PR153 config, scanner, watcher, and their added source-admission controls
